title: Gamma Cygni Nebula (Sadr Region)
description: A diffuse emission nebula and H II region surrounding the star Sadr (Gamma Cygni), which marks the center of the Northern Cross asterism in Cygnus.

title: Dumbbell Nebula
description: One of the brightest planetary nebulae in the sky, formed from the outer layers of gas shed by a dying star in the constellation Vulpecula.

title: Cooling Tower Cluster
description: A compact open star cluster in Cygnus, roughly 4,000 light-years away, containing a handful of hot, young, blue stars.

title: Messier 56
description: A moderately dense globular cluster in the constellation Lyra, located roughly 33,000 light-years from Earth.

title: Messier 71
description: A loosely concentrated globular cluster in the small constellation Sagitta, once debated as either a dense open cluster or a sparse globular cluster.

title: Messier 75
description: A compact, highly concentrated globular cluster in Sagittarius, around 67,500 light-years away.

title: Eastern Veil Nebula
description: The brightest part of the Eastern half of the Veil Nebula, a large supernova remnant in Cygnus left behind by a star that exploded 10,000-20,000 years ago.

title: Crab Nebula
description: A supernova remnant in Taurus from a star whose explosion was observed on Earth in 1054 AD; it now hosts the fast-spinning Crab Pulsar at its center.

title: Messier 4
description: A loose, relatively nearby globular cluster in Scorpius, one of the easiest globulars to resolve into individual stars with modest equipment.

title: Lagoon Nebula
description: A large emission nebula and active star-forming region in Sagittarius, bright enough to be glimpsed with the naked eye under dark skies.

title: Great Globular Cluster in Hercules
description: One of the brightest globular clusters visible from the northern hemisphere, containing several hundred thousand stars packed into a sphere about 145 light-years across.

title: Eagle Nebula
description: A young emission nebula and star cluster in Serpens, famous for the towering "Pillars of Creation" columns of gas and dust.

title: Omega Nebula (Swan Nebula)
description: A bright emission nebula and star-forming region in Sagittarius, also known as the Swan or Horseshoe Nebula for its distinctive shape.

title: Trifid Nebula
description: A striking combination of an emission nebula, a reflection nebula, and a dark nebula in Sagittarius, split into lobes by dark dust lanes.

title: Messier 22
description: A large, bright globular cluster in Sagittarius and one of the closest globulars to Earth.

title: Pleiades (Seven Sisters)
description: A prominent open cluster of hot, young, blue stars in Taurus, wrapped in a faint reflection nebula and visible to the naked eye.

title: Messier 86
description: A lenticular galaxy near the core of the Virgo Cluster, one of the largest and brightest members of that cluster.

title: Messier 94
description: A tightly-wound spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici, known for a bright inner ring of active star formation.

title: Sombrero Galaxy
description: A spiral galaxy in Virgo with an unusually large central bulge and a prominent dust lane, giving it the look of a wide-brimmed hat.

title: NGC 2420
description: An open cluster of stars in Gemini roughly 10,000 light-years away, discovered by William Herschel in 1783.

title: NGC 5033
description: An inclined spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici with a bright, active galactic nucleus.

title: Splinter Galaxy
description: An edge-on spiral galaxy in Draco, also called the Knife Edge Galaxy, known for a faint surrounding stellar stream from a cannibalized satellite galaxy.

title: Cat's Paw Nebula
description: A large emission nebula and star-forming region in Scorpius, named for the pattern of glowing lobes resembling a cat's paw print.

title: V488 Sagittae
description: A variable star in the small constellation Sagitta.

title: Saturn
description: The ringed gas giant, sixth planet from the Sun.

title: Aldebaran
description: An orange giant star marking the eye of the bull in Taurus, and one of the brightest stars in the night sky.

title: Betelgeuse
description: A red supergiant marking the shoulder of Orion, one of the largest and most luminous stars visible to the naked eye.

title: Procyon
description: A bright binary star system in Canis Minor and one of the closest stars to the Sun.

title: The Moon
description: Earth's only natural satellite.

title: Jupiter
description: The largest planet in the Solar System, a gas giant known for its Great Red Spot and large family of moons.

title: Venus
description: The second planet from the Sun, similar in size to Earth but shrouded in a thick, hot, toxic atmosphere.
